en.headline: Government aims to make Smart Site Safety System standard on all construction sites
en.dek: Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said accident rates fell about 20 per cent from 2023 to 2025 as adoption of the 4S system reached roughly 80 per cent of local sites.
body: Authorities on Monday pledged to make the Smart Site Safety System the standard configuration for all construction sites in Hong Kong as part of a zero-tolerance approach to workplace accidents.

Speaking at the kick-off of Construction Safety Week, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said overall accident rates had dropped by roughly 20 per cent between 2023 and 2025, largely attributed to wider use of the 4S system, now installed at about 80 per cent of sites, with 60 per cent earning the official 4S label.

She said the Development Bureau had updated technical guidelines last month to add three new categories of 4S devices covering high-risk processes on public works. Construction Industry Council chairman Thomas Ho noted 15 fatal accidents had already been recorded this year, matching the full-year total for 2025, and urged stakeholders to address a persistent “rush” culture on sites.

zh.headline: 政府推動智慧工地安全系統成全港工地標準配置
zh.dek: 發展局局長甯漢豪表示，建造業意外率由2023至2025年下降約兩成，智慧工地安全系統已安裝於約八成本地工地。
body: 當局周一表示，目標是令智慧工地安全系統成為全港所有建造工地的標準配置，以零容忍態度處理工地意外。
發展局局長甯漢豪在建造業安全周啟動儀式上表示，建造業整體意外率由2023年至2025年期間下降約20%，主要歸功於智慧工地安全系統（4S）的廣泛應用，目前約八成本地工地已安裝，其中六成獲發正式標籤。
她指發展局上月更新技術指引，新增三類4S設備以涵蓋工務工程高風險工序。建造業議會主席何安誠指出，今年已錄得15宗致命意外，與去年全年數字相同，並呼籲業界正視工地「趕工」文化。
